newsitem.title: UK: Somerfield posts higher sales and profits.
newsitem.headline: Somerfield posts higher sales and profits.

text.p: British food retailer Somerfield Plc said on Tuesday there had been marked improvement in its performance, paving the way for future expansion, as it unveiled its first results since flotation last August.

Pretax profit in the 28 weeks to November 9, 1996 were 54.6 million pounds ($90.68 million), up from 43.0 million while sales rose 1.3 percent to 1.71 billion pounds from 1.69 billion. The company said its like for like sales rose four percent in the first nine weeks of the second half.
Chief executive David Simons said, "The strength of our financial performance and our greatly increased investment capacity provide Somerfield with a solid base for future expansion."

The group, created in one of the big leveraged-buyouts of the 1980s, is in the process of converting its old Gateway stores into the new-style Somerfield format and has so far converted 74 percent of its selling space.

Sales in Somerfield stores in the half year were up 4.3 percent, while sales in the unconverted shops fell 5.5 percent. Its Food Giant stores suffered a six percent drop in sales, which the group said was disappointing.

The group expects to convert a further 20 stores in the current year, and spend 107 million pounds over the year mainly on store refurbishment. The retailer proposed a dividend of 3.4 pence. ($1=.6021 Pound)
